subject: DPA sequencing and transfer safeguards for Helios — SCCs, UK Addendum, TIA
messages:
From: Alex Morris <alex.morris@helioslabs.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Question: DPA exhibits and UK Addendum sequencing

Hi Connor,

Thanks for the deck this morning — Helios legal and compliance had a quick question about sequencing. We need to understand how Redwood expects to handle the EU SCCs + UK Addendum situation for our contract. Specifically: 

- Should we sign the EU SCCs first and then attach the UK Addendum as an exhibit (UK IDTA), or do you deliver a combined DPA that has SCCs + UK Addendum embedded?
- We have a small TIA (transfers impact assessment) requirement for our privacy team that maps data flows to safeguards. Will Redwood provide a mapping/template, or do we need to run that internally?
- Procurement will need a DocuSign route and an expected signature ETA. They prefer a 7–10 day turnaround from final DPA.

Can you loop in legal if needed and confirm the recommended path so we can align our internal teams?

Appreciate it — Alex

--
Alex Morris
Head of Security & Privacy, Helios Labs
alex.morris@helioslabs.com

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morris <alex.morris@helioslabs.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 15:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Question: DPA exhibits and UK Addendum sequencing

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up-front, then a proposed sequencing and attachments.

Summary recommendation (Redwood position):
1) We typically issue a single DPA package: core DPA + EU SCCs incorporated as an exhibit + separate UK Addendum (UK IDTA) attached as a signed exhibit. This keeps each legal instrument explicit for auditors while making signature flow straightforward.
2) We provide a starter TIA scope/mapping template (attached) that outlines our processing flows, subprocessors, and where technical safeguards (onshore cache, region routing, KMS) apply. You can use it to complete your side and we’ll fill the columns relating to Redwood controls.
3) DocuSign: we can prepare the package for signature once commercial terms are agreed. Typical procurement ETA: 5–10 business days from final DPA sent. For accelerated timelines we can do a canary-sign approach (SCCs + core DPA first, then UK exhibit signed as addendum within the same DocuSign envelope).

Proposed sequencing (detailed):
- Day 0: Redwood sends DPA package (Redwood_DPA_v4.3.pdf) + Subprocessor list + TIA_scope_template.xlsx (we’re attaching both).
- Day 0–2: Helios legal reviews; list any redlines to the core DPA language or SCCs.
- Day 2–5: Redwood legal (cc Kimberly) reviews redlines; we try to limit changes to exhibits.
- Day 5: Final DPA package to DocuSign (SCCs in-line, UK Addendum attached as separate exhibit).
- Day 5–12: Signature window (target 7 business days).

Notes on routing and TIA:
- We can commit to region-routing policies and will document expected processing regions in the TIA mapping. For production inference, we offer onshore cache and explicit routing policies; any permanent routing to the US requires customer opt-in. Temporary fallbacks (for capacity/DR) are spelled out in the DPA exhibit and can be restricted by route policy.

Kimberly — I’m looping you in for legal confirmation on the combined-package approach and the fallback wording.

Alex — attaching: Redwood_DPA_v4.3.pdf, Redwood_subprocessors_list_202806.pdf, TIA_scope_template.xlsx. Also including a DocuSign preview link in related links. Let me know procurement contact and any timing constraints.

Thanks,
Connor
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
--
Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v4.3.pdf (PDF), Redwood_subprocessors_list_202806.pdf (PDF), TIA_scope_template.xlsx (Spreadsheet)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morris <alex.morris@helioslabs.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Jun 2028 10:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Question: DPA exhibits and UK Addendum sequencing

Hi Alex / team — happy to confirm and add a couple of legal specifics.

1) Packaging: we prefer a single envelope with the core DPA (with SCCs) and an attached UK Addendum exhibit that is referenced by the core DPA. That gives auditors and your privacy team a clear chain: core obligations -> international transfer mechanism -> UK-specific supplement.

2) Subprocessors: the attached Redwood_subprocessors_list_202806.pdf is the current snapshot. For signature we mark it as "current as of execution date" and include a 30-day notice period for material subprocessor changes. If Helios requires prior notification or explicit approval for certain subprocessors, note those providers during review and we can add a carve-out.

3) UK Addendum specifics: the UK IDTA language we use is consistent with the latest Home Office guidance; we can provide a version with the additional demonstrable safeguards section (we leave that optional but recommended in regulated contexts).

4) TIA: Redwood will populate the technical controls columns (encryption at-rest/in-transit, KMS custody, logging/audit retention, telemetry scoping). Helios should populate the data classification and retention obligations to ensure the mapping is complete.

5) Routing & fallback commitments: permanent cross-border routing restrictions need to be explicitly documented in the DPA. We can commit to a default operational policy that production inference traffic for Helios remains routed to EU regions unless Helios enables multi-region fallback. Emergency fallbacks (capacity/DR) are limited to time-boxed events and require notification; we will include a max-time cap in the exhibit.

If procurement can send the exact contact and any PO terms (e.g., required insurance limits, local invoicing), Laura can coordinate the commercial signature window.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security — Redwood Inference

From: Alex Morris <alex.morris@helioslabs.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, procurement@helioslabs.com
Date: Wed, 6 Jun 2028 14:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Question: DPA exhibits and UK Addendum sequencing

Thanks Connor and Kimberly — that works for us. Procurement (procurement@helioslabs.com) is the signer; they expect a single DocuSign envelope if possible. They also asked for a short appendix confirming:

- Redwood will not route production inference traffic outside the EU except where Helios explicitly opts in.
- Any emergency fallback to non-EU regions will be preceded by notice and limited to 72 hours unless otherwise agreed.

One quick clarification on the onshore cache note: can you provide the column in the TIA template that shows where onshore cache is used and whether cached tokens are persistently stored outside the EU? If the column is available we’ll fill in the Helios side and return.

If you can provide the updated TIA mapping sample and confirm the DocuSign envelope ETA, we’ll queue procurement for signature.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Alex
